_note: The player's front door drops them on (18,24) and loadMap resets lastTile, so the landing tile itself never fires a step script -- the trigger has to be every tile they can reach from it, and there are exactly three: west, east and south. (18,23) is the door back inside. Tarin waits on his own doorstep at (13,24), two doors west, and runs east to (16,24), so (16,24) and (17,24) must stay clear of scenery -- scripted movers ignore collision and he would otherwise finish standing inside a flower bed. THE EXIT: west two, then straight up the street. He does NOT walk all the way to the station: it is twenty tiles and a bridge away, and a scripted run that long is a minute of the player watching somebody else's back. He is off the top of a 240x160 view by the time he reaches the square, and the line after the move is what reports the rest of it.

lines: FINALLY. {name}. I have been stood on my own doorstep since it was dark.
Saffra came past with a bucket and asked twice if I was locked out.
Sorrell has three of them over the bridge. Three. Sat up on the counter, in the open, like a bowl of apples.
I have not touched them. I want it on record that I have not touched them.
Well? Are you coming or not?
Yes. Good. Right. Try to keep up.
Absolutely not, it is your day.
I have had mine explained to me since I was four. Yours is still yours.
Tarin. Ashe. That house. Sixteen years, two gardens between us, one fence I put through.
...Unbelievable. Come on.
Tarin is across the square and over the bridge before you have moved.

_note2: THE CODA. After Tarin goes, the script warps the player home and has their mother put the party back together. This is the game's only teaching pass on where healing happens, and it is deliberately not a line of instruction: the first battle is also the first time the player's kin are hurt, so being taken home and fixed at exactly that moment is the lesson. The landing tile is (5,5), directly below the mother's (5,4), and the player faces up -- so the pair are face to face on the frame the fade lifts with nobody having to walk. NOBODY WALKS HERE ON PURPOSE. `move who:"player"` cannot be used inside a cutscene at all: the player body is only ticked by updatePlayer, which overworld.update skips for the whole time an event is running, so a scripted player walk never completes and hangs the script. Moving the mother is possible but would name an NPC from another map inside a hearthmere script, which tests/content.test.js rejects. Standing them where they need to be is cheaper than either. mom_rest is set here rather than left to her own script, which hands her 'interact' dialogue straight to the repeatable 'Do you want to rest before you go?' branch -- so the very next time the player talks to her, the thing they were just shown is offered again on a button press. The healParty is followed by a wait because healParty does not block; see OverworldEventHost.healParty.
_note: Fires on the station forecourt. The player lands on (21,5) coming out of the double door; (21,4) is the door back in, so the only three tiles they can step to are west, east and south, and all three are listed. Tarin is NOT on the map at this point: hm_tarin_meet ran removeNpc on him and its onceFlag hides him for good, which is why this scene used to be delivered by a disembodied voice with nobody on screen. He is spawned again on the far bank at (25,10) and comes UP THE PLANK FOOTBRIDGE into frame before a word is said, and he leaves the same way. That route is chosen because scripted movers ignore collision: the forecourt is three rows deep and a run across it would pass straight through wherever the player happens to be standing, whereas the bridge column x=25 is the one line they cannot be on. The removeNpc before the spawn is belt and braces: spawnNpc is a no-op if an actor with that id already exists.

lines: {name}. HEY. Don't you dare walk off up that road yet.
Sorrell gave me one too. I picked mine on looks and I have since been shown a chart.
Apparently there is an order to them, and mine is at the wrong end of it from yours.
I have decided that is a detail and not a problem.
One battle. Right here. Before either of us knows what we are doing.
THERE it is.
Exactly. That is the only moment this is ever going to be fair.
In a month you will be insufferable. Fight me now.

actions._note: Tarin takes the starter the PLAYER'S beats -- see docs/TARIN.md and the $comment on tarin_first_* in data/trainers/trainers.json. The branch names TARIN'S kin, not the player's: Sprigling beats Rilltail beats Cinderpaw beats Sprigling.

lines: Right. Yes. The chart was not a detail. The chart was the whole thing.
Noted. Written down. Look at the state of yours, though — I got something out of that.
HA. With the bad end of the chart and everything.
Sorry. I am not sorry. Go on, get them patched up before you fall over.
Listen, {name}, before you go. There were people on the north road last week.
Grey coats, brass instruments, very polite. Meridian, the badges said.
They were not measuring the road. They were kneeling on it, measuring what is underneath.
My mother keeps a Kin Hall two regions off. She has never once sounded frightened on paper.
Her last letter asked whether the sea near you had stopped moving too.
...Go. Fill Sorrell's book. I will see you up the road.
Tarin is back over the plank bridge and away along the bank before you can answer.
That took more out of them than you expected.
The house is five minutes back down the street, over the bridge and past the well.
Back already? You have not even been gone an hour.
...Oh. Oh, come here.
Give them here. Don't argue with me about it.
There. Warm, cross, and entirely fine.
{name}. This house does not move, and neither do I.
Whenever they get into that state, you bring them home. I will do that again. Every time.
Now go. Tarin will be halfway up Route 1 telling people he won.

_note:
STAGE 7, THE ENDING, BEAT 1: COMING DOWN THE ROAD.

THE WHOLE ENDING IS THE OPENING WALK, BACKWARDS. data/maps/hearthmere.json says so in its own _plan -- 'out of the front door, west along the lane, north up the street past everyone who knows you, over the water, to the station. Coming home reverses it.' So nothing here warps the player through the village. They arrive at the top of the road and they walk the length of it, past seven people whose lines have all changed, to somebody standing on their doorstep.

WHY IT IS A STEP TRIGGER ON THE ROAD AND NOT AN `enter` ON THE MAP. An enter script fires however the player got here, including out of their own front door, and 'you have never come down this road before' is a lie the second time. The `at` list is the six tiles of the road between the wood and the mill field, so it can only fire on somebody walking in from Route 1 -- or on somebody the Summit put down at (14,1), whose first step is (14,2).

THE MUSIC. Stopped for two boxes and then put back. town_hearth has not been heard since Act 1 for most players and it is the only thing in the ending that does not need writing.

GATE: `champion`. See the handover at the top of hm_end_mira.

lines: Four hundred souls, one bridge, one road.
You have been up it once. This is the first time you have come down it.
Somebody down by the mere has already seen you and is running, badly, in clogs.

_note:
STAGE 7, THE ENDING, BEAT 2: MIRA.

CANON 64: 'The player returns to Hearthmere. Mira is waiting.' She is waiting on the tile the player stepped onto leaving this house in Act 1, so she is standing in the doorway of the scene as well as the house. The trigger tiles are the three that touch (18,24) from the lane and the meadow, which is every way in; she occupies the door tile itself, so there is no route past her.

SHE HAS SPENT THE WHOLE GAME BEING AFRAID AND NOT LETTING IT SHOW. This is the one scene where she does not have to, and the writing rule for it is that she is allowed to fail at being brisk rather than allowed to make a speech. Four boxes, a choice that mirrors the three-option choice she opens the game with, and she goes back inside first -- because Act 1 ends this lane with somebody else running off up the street and leaving the player standing on it.

THE THREE OPTIONS ARE ALL CORRECT. The middle one is the region map she handed over in Act 1 ('Here. Your father's.'), which the player has been carrying for the entire game.

WHAT THIS RELIES ON SOMEBODY ELSE PROVIDING:
  - THE FLAG `champion`, set the moment the Champion of Caelora is beaten. `act7_done` is
    accepted as an alias by hm_end_road; this scene and the NPC's own requiresFlag can only
    read one, so `champion` is the contract. It is also set by the shared script
    `ending_go_home` in data/events/common.json, which is the one-line handoff the Summit
    should use: it fades, sets the flag and puts the player at the top of the Hearthmere road.
  - NOTHING ELSE. If the Summit never calls that script, the player walks home themselves and
    every scene in the ending still fires in order.

WHAT IT PROVIDES: `ending_home`, which hides hm_mira_door and opens the interior scene in data/events/hearthmere_house_player.json.

lines: She is on the doorstep with a tea towel in her hand and she has not moved for a while.
Do not stand in the lane, {name}. The whole street is at their windows.
...No. Stand there. Let me look at you first.
Sixteen years at that window. I have got very good at that road.
It has never once had you on it coming this way.
I am not going to manage this quietly. I have been trying since four o'clock.
Well? Say something. You have had a whole region to think of something.
Yes.
Yes. All right. Yes.
It was your father's and then it was yours and I am not having it back.
Look at the state of it. Look at the state of you.
Neither of you says anything for a while. The tea towel is in a knot.
Right. Right.
Come in. The kettle has been on since four and it has been off twice.
She leaves the door open behind her.

_note:
STAGE 7, THE ENDING, BEAT 5: TARIN COMES BACK.

CANON 64: 'Tarin comes back too, eventually.' Eventually is the operative word and it is why he is gated on `tideheart_home` rather than on the homecoming -- the study is a room the player goes into alone, and he must not be standing in the lane while they do it.

IT IS THE SAME SCENE AS hm_tarin_meet, DELIBERATELY, DOWN TO THE TILES. Same three trigger tiles, same doorstep at (13,24), the same three-step run east to (16,24), the same opening word, the same tic about wanting things on record, the same three-option choice, and the same '...Unbelievable.' if the player says nothing. The one thing that is different is where he goes at the end of it: in Act 1 he runs north up the road and off the top of the screen, and here he walks west along the lane and in through his own front door at (10,23), which he has not done in the whole game.

HE DOES NOT ASK FOR A BATTLE. The last rival battle is the Ascent's and it has already happened by the time this fires; canon has him go quiet when it is serious, and the quiet version of the thing he wants is the last two boxes.

WHAT IT PROVIDES: `ending_tarin`, which hides him and opens the last scene in data/events/hearthmere_house_up.json.

lines: FINALLY.
Do you have any idea how far that is on foot when the wireless has already told everybody?
I have been on your gate about ninety seconds and I want that on record.
So. Champion of Caelora.
It was not close. I have had it described to me four times on the way here.
It got less close every single time.
Yes.
...Yes. That is the plan and I have said it out loud now, so that is that.
No, go on. I have walked eleven miles for this. Say something insufferable.
You do not.
...Unbelievable.
I am not going to ask you for a battle.
I have thought about it the whole way here and I am not going to ask. Not tonight.
Tomorrow. Up the road. Same as we did it the first time.

actions._note: Down onto the meadow verge for three tiles and back up, because the roofer stands at (12,24) once act6_done is set and scripted movers ignore collision -- a straight run west would walk Tarin through a man on a ladder.

lines: The Ashes' front door bangs. It has banged like that since you were four.
It is nearly dark. Somebody has put the upstairs light on.
